methods.label: Translate the progressions into tangent equations
methods.explanation:
The altitude of an isosceles triangle also bisects its base and vertex angle. Thus \(AD=DC\) and \(\angle ABD=\angle DBC\). This symmetry lets us express all three angles in the geometric progression using just two angles.

[Figure 1](figures/2004_AMC_12B_Q24_question_fig1.svg)

Let
\[
\alpha=\angle DBC,\qquad
\beta=\angle DBE,\qquad
x=\tan\alpha,\quad y=\tan\beta.
\]
Since \(E\) is beyond \(C\), we have \(0<\alpha<\beta<90^\circ\), so \(0<x<y\). Also,
\[
\angle CBE=\beta-\alpha,
\qquad \angle ABE=\beta+\alpha.
\]
The tangent addition and subtraction formulas give
\[
\tan\angle CBE=\frac{y-x}{1+xy},
\qquad
\tan\angle ABE=\frac{y+x}{1-xy}.
\]
All the stated tangents must be defined. The first two terms of the geometric progression are positive, so its common ratio and third term are positive as well. Since \(y+x>0\), this forces \(1-xy>0\). Thus the denominators used below are nonzero.

The square of the middle term of a geometric progression equals the product of its neighbors. Therefore
\[
y^2=\frac{y-x}{1+xy}\cdot\frac{y+x}{1-xy}
=\frac{y^2-x^2}{1-x^2y^2}.
\]
Clearing the nonzero denominator and canceling \(y^2\) gives
\[
x^2y^4=x^2.
\]
Because \(x>0\), we obtain \(y^4=1\); because \(y>0\), we obtain \(y=1\). Consequently \(0<x<1\).

Now use the arithmetic progression. Cotangent is the reciprocal of tangent for these nonzero values, so its three terms are
\[
1,\qquad \frac{1+x}{1-x},\qquad \frac1x.
\]
The middle term is the average of the other two:
\[
2\frac{1+x}{1-x}=1+\frac1x
=\frac{1+x}{x}.
\]
Here \(x>0\), \(1-x>0\), and \(1+x>0\), so cancellation and multiplication give \(2x=1-x\), hence \(x=1/3\).

Let \(h=BD\). The right triangles give \(DC=xh=h/3\) and \(DE=yh=h\). By the Pythagorean theorem,
\[
100=BE^2=BD^2+DE^2=2h^2,
\qquad h^2=50.
\]
The resulting tangent terms are \(1/2,1,2\), and the cotangent terms are \(1,2,3\), verifying both original progressions. Finally, \(AC=2DC\), so
\[
\operatorname{Area}(ABC)
=\frac12(2DC)BD
=\frac{h^2}{3}
=\frac{50}{3}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\dfrac{50}{3}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
